description: A recovery flow artifact is valid when every failure state has a declared recovery action, critical failures provide escape routes, retry counts are bounded, backoff is declared for multi-retry paths, and user-facing error messages are specific and actionable.

rules.description: recovery-flow-spec.json must exist with a failures array. Features without a recovery spec have undefined error behavior.
The failures array must contain at least one entry. A recovery flow compiler with no failures has nothing to enforce.
All failure ids must be unique within the spec. Duplicate ids create ambiguous recovery routing.
Every failure must declare a recovery object with at least one of: retry, redirect, fallback, or contactSupport. An empty recovery leaves users stranded.
Failures with severity=critical or fatal must declare an escapeHatch (string action id). Users in critical failure states must have a path back to safety.
Failures with triggers containing 'offline' or 'network' must declare a fallback. Offline users need a degraded but functional experience.
Any recovery with retry:true must declare maxRetries between 1 and 10. Infinite retry loops degrade servers and frustrate users.
Recoveries with retry:true and maxRetries > 1 must declare backoff as linear, exponential, or fixed. Rapid-fire retries without backoff can cause cascading server failures.
Every failure must declare a userMessage that is specific and actionable. Generic messages like 'Something went wrong' give users no recovery information.
version must be declared for change tracking and spec migration.
